data.description:
## Description

What: Add a CodeQL analysis job to .github/workflows/ci.yml, PR-triggered, that initializes CodeQL for the repo's languages, runs the analysis, and uploads results to GitHub's code-scanning API. Why: This is the walking skeleton — the code-scanning data this job emits is the precondition for the Require CodeQL ruleset rule to be enableable without permanently blocking PRs. Scope IN: the CodeQL workflow job (init/analyze/upload) on pull_request events. Scope OUT: enabling the ruleset rule (draft-4), the synthetic gating demonstration (draft-5), code-quality SARIF (draft-2).


## Done Definitions

- On a PR, the CodeQL job in .github/workflows/ci.yml runs to completion and produces a code-scanning analysis visible via the code-scanning API for that PR's head SHA ← Satisfies: sc-1
- The code-scanning API reports at least the most recent CodeQL analysis for the repository after a PR run ← Satisfies: sc-1
- The CodeQL job triggers on all pull_request events with no path/branch filter that would drop a PR, and a PR that touches no analyzable code still reports a terminal (success or neutral) CodeQL check conclusion rather than leaving a missing/permanently-pending required check ← Satisfies: sc-1

## Considerations

- [Security] CodeQL requires the security-events: write permission on the job; ensure the workflow grants it without over-broadening the default token scope.
- [Performance] CodeQL analysis is slow; consider matrix/language scoping so PR latency stays acceptable.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a security maintainer, I want a CodeQL job on every PR uploading to the code-scanning API, so that security findings surface as gateable check results.
